t: You're looking at the Harold Pinter Theatre on Panton Street, a West End theatre that opened in October 1881 as the Royal Comedy Theatre. Thomas Verity designed it, and it was built in just six months. It was known as the Comedy Theatre until 2011, when it took the name of Harold Pinter. Pinter was a playwright and a Nobel Prize winner in 2005, and his best-known plays include The Birthday Party, The Homecoming and Betrayal. After a major rebuild in the mid-1950s, the auditorium remains essentially that of 1881, with three tiers of horseshoe-shaped balconies.
